questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Nepal?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nepal article.

questions.proof: Kathmandu is Nepal's capital and biggest city.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Nepal?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Nepal on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nepal article.

questions.proof: It's bordered by China to the north and India to the south, east, and west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Nepal?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nepal article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It's close to Bangladesh and _____, separated by small strips of land.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “separated”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nepal article.

questions.proof: It's close to Bangladesh and Bhutan, separated by small strips of land.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In September _____, protests against social media ban, economic inequality and corruption caused riots, resulting in casualties and the resignation of the prime minister.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nepal article.

questions.proof: In September 2025, protests against social media ban, economic inequality and corruption caused riots, resulting in casualties and the resignation of the prime minister.
